## Summary

First M3 slice: a small, presentation-independent, well-tested C++20 facade for reading
Project Ignis `.cdb` card databases, in a new `data/` module. This becomes the authoritative
card-data boundary for the deck model, card search, and QML deck builder to build on later -
none of that is implemented yet. It is not part of the duel rules engine and makes no
legality decisions.

Only "Card database facade" from M3's roadmap list is done in this PR. Deck model, fast
search, and the QML deck builder are explicitly not started.

**Update (locale correction pass):** external review found a confirmed state-loss bug in the
original locale design - `load_locale()` wrote translated text directly into the only stored
record, so a base string a locale had overwritten had no way back, and switching locales (or
returning to the base language) could not restore it. Fixing it required re-tracing the real
upstream locale lifecycle end to end (`Game::ApplyLocale`,
`DataManager::ClearLocaleTexts`/`ParseLocaleDB`, `CardDataM::GetStrings`/`GetDesc`), which also
surfaced that the original PR's per-field name/text fallback was an invented rule, not
upstream's actual (asymmetric) one. Both are corrected below; the sections that described the
old design have been rewritten, not just appended to.

## Architecture

- New top-level `data/` module (own `CMakeLists.txt`, standalone like `client/`/`ui/`),
  depending on the C++20 standard library and SQLite (via CMake's own `find_package(SQLite3)`
  against the system package, not the project's vcpkg bundle) - and nothing else. It does not
  include `client/`, `gframe/`, `ocgcore/`, or the legacy `DataManager`; `sqlite3.h` never
  appears in `data/include/`.
- `edopro_next_client` is unchanged and still builds with no SQLite/card-data dependency
  (verified locally, see Validation).
- `CardDatabase` keeps three maps internally: `base_text_` (the base text layer - a
  successful `load_database()` call may replace it for a code, but no locale operation ever
  touches it), `locale_text_` (the active locale layer, discarded whole by `clear_locale()`), and
  `records_` (the materialized effective view `find()`/iteration expose). `find()`'s pointer
  stays valid for the object's lifetime, but is not a snapshot - see the header's own
  pointer/reference-stability note.
- Full rationale for the module boundary, the SQLite provisioning choice, load atomicity, the
  locale layer design, and the card-code-0 invariant is in
  [`docs/adr/0003-card-database-facade.md`](docs/adr/0003-card-database-facade.md) (5
  decisions).

## Upstream source research

Read from `gframe/data_manager.h`/`.cpp` (the `.cdb` schema, every field transformation
`DataManager::ParseDB` applies, and the full locale lifecycle -
`ParseLocaleDB`/`ClearLocaleTexts`/`GetStrings`/`GetDesc`), `gframe/data_handler.cpp` and
`gframe/game.cpp` (real database/locale load order, and `Game::ApplyLocale`'s clear-then-load
sequence), and `gframe/deck_manager.cpp`/`deck.h` (what fields downstream deck logic actually
consumes, and the code-0 dummy-entry convention) - written up with source citations in
[`docs/architecture/card-database.md`](docs/architecture/card-database.md).

Key findings baked into the design:

- The base query is an inner join between `datas` and `texts`; a card missing from either
  table is not loaded at all - reproduced exactly.
- Loading multiple databases is unconditional last-file-wins per card code, verified against
  `ParseDB`'s own `cards[code]` overwrite and against real load order
  (`cards.cdb`, then every `expansions/*.cdb`, then archives).
- Link monsters store their link-marker bitmask in the `def` column, and their real defense
  is always 0 - reproduced exactly, using the Link type bit cited from `ocgcore`'s own public
  header (`ocgcore/ocgapi_constants.h:58`), not copied from `gframe/`.
- Level and Pendulum scale share one packed, signed int, and the sign of the *whole* value -
  not just the low byte - determines the decoded intermediate result's sign. But
  `CardData::level`/`CardDataC::level` (and the engine-facing `OCG_CardData::level` they are
  memcpy'd into unchanged) are `uint32_t`, not `int32_t` - so `CardRecord::level` is
  `uint32_t` too, and a negative intermediate result is stored as the wrapped unsigned value,
  matching upstream's own observable deck-search level filter (`gframe/deck_con.cpp`), which
  compares this field as `uint32_t`. Traced bit-for-bit and covered by a test with a
  genuinely negative packed value: `level = -249` gives a signed intermediate of `-7`, stored
  and exposed as `static_cast<uint32_t>(-7)` == `4294967289` (`0xfffffff9`); scales come out
  `255`/`255` as a mechanical side effect of sign extension.
- Race is read as a true 64-bit value in upstream too, not a modern extension this PR
  invented.
- **Locale lifecycle** (`Game::ApplyLocale`, `gframe/game.cpp:3987-4020`): `ClearLocaleTexts()`
  runs unconditionally before loading any newly selected locale, including before returning to
  the base language, which loads nothing at all.
  `CardDataM::GetStrings()` links `name`/`text` as a pair - once a locale is linked for a code,
  both come from the locale layer even if one is empty, never falling back to base
  field-by-field; only the sixteen auxiliary strings (`CardDataM::GetDesc()`) fall back per
  slot. `ParseLocaleDB` reuses `locales[code]` across every file loaded into one active locale,
  and `GetWstring` unconditionally clears a field with no value - so a later file's row for a
  code an earlier file in the same active locale already touched replaces it completely, even
  with an empty value.
- 0 is upstream's own synthesized "not a real card" sentinel
  (`CardDataC::getRealCode()`, `DeckManager`'s dummy entries), never a real `.cdb` row in
  practice.

One remaining deliberate, documented divergence (explained with source citations in the ADR,
Decision 4): a locale row for a card code not already loaded via `load_database()` is ignored,
rather than queued for order-independent linking - verified that upstream's own real call
sites never load locale before base, so that upstream capability is real but dead code in
practice.

## Card record / public API

`CardRecord` (code, alias, scope, setcodes, type, attack, defense, level, left/right scale,
race, attribute, category, link_marker, name, text, 16 auxiliary strings) - UTF-8
`std::string` throughout, fixed-width integers, no `std::wstring`/Irrlicht/`epro::*` types,
no presentation formatting.

`CardDatabase`: `load_database()`/`load_locale()` (read-only, atomic - a file that fails
partway through leaves the *relevant layer* exactly as it was before the call, for the base
layer and the active locale layer independently, which is a stronger guarantee than
`DataManager::ParseDB`/`ParseLocaleDB` themselves give), `clear_locale()` (discards the active
locale layer and restores base text; harmless when none is active), `find()`, `contains()`,
`size()`, and deterministic ascending-by-code iteration via `begin()`/`end()`. No fast search
yet, no SQLite types anywhere in the public API.

## Testing

`data/tests/test_card_database.cpp` builds tiny synthetic SQLite databases at runtime with
the real `datas`/`texts` table layout - **no committed `.cdb`, artwork, or CardScripts**,
and no copied card text, per CLAUDE.md. 30 cases, deterministic, no network access:

- ordinary decode, UTF-8 names/text, negative attack/defense, positive and negative packed
  level with Pendulum scale, the Link monster defense/link-marker swap, a 64-bit race value,
  packed setcodes (including all-zero and with-gaps), aliases, all 16 auxiliary strings, the
  inner-join exclusion, missing-card lookup, deterministic enumeration, last-database-wins
  across a duplicate code, card-code-0 rejection;
- locale: name/text linked as a pair (not per-field fallback), per-slot auxiliary-string
  fallback, `clear_locale()` restoring base strings, clearing then switching to a different
  locale (proving no cross-locale leakage), multiple locale files within *one* active locale
  taking last-file-wins precedence (kept as a distinct test from switching locales, so the two
  can't be conflated), a base reload while a locale is active (the overlay stays applied, and
  an empty auxiliary slot falls back to the *newly* reloaded base value, not a stale one), an
  unknown-code locale row being ignored, `clear_locale()` as a harmless no-op with nothing
  active;
- six failure paths: missing file, non-SQLite file, two shapes of incompatible schema, that a
  failed `load_database()` leaves a previously-loaded catalogue untouched, and that a failed
  `load_locale()` leaves the *active locale* untouched.

No test framework dependency, matching `client/`'s own choice and reasoning (ADR 0002,
Decision 4) - a fresh copy of that tiny harness, not an include of `client/tests/`, since
`data/` has no other reason to reference `client/` at all.

CI job `card-database`, in the same cheap every-push tier as `semantic-client` (apt-installed
`libsqlite3-dev`, no vcpkg).

## Validation

- **Card database facade tests:** built and ran locally (WSL, per `docs/BASELINE.md`'s own
  "copy off `/mnt/c` first" guidance) against the vcpkg-provided SQLite headers/lib already
  cached from a previous baseline build - `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`, all 30 cases
  pass, zero warnings. Current-head CI (`card-database` job) confirms the same on a clean
  runner.
- **`client/` unit tests:** built and ran locally (WSL, full-tree sync so `integration/legacy`
  resolves correctly) - all 7 CTest suites pass, unaffected, confirming `edopro_next_client`
  still has no SQLite/card-data dependency.
- **Python regression suite:** `tools/generate_messages.py --check`,
  `tools/generate_protocol_constants.py --check`, and the full `unittest discover` (33 tests)
  all pass locally.
- **Semantic goldens:** re-verified with `test_semantic_trace.py --require` against a
  freshly-built `edopro_next_semantic_trace` (matches the committed goldens exactly) -
  confirming this correction pass has zero effect on the M2 semantic decoder.
- **`git diff --check`:** clean, no whitespace errors.
- **Qt shell:** not built locally (no local Qt 6 install); relying on the `qt-shell` CI job,
  which this PR does not touch.
- **Full diff audit:** confirmed no changes under `ocgcore/` or `gframe/`, no `.cdb`/artwork/
  script files, no build artifacts, no accidental files.

## Known limitations / deliberately deferred

- No fast search, no deck model, no `.ydk` reading/writing, no QML deck builder, no
  legality/banlist logic, no card artwork/image handling - all explicitly out of scope for
  this slice.
- No locale name, language code, or file-discovery logic in this module - `load_locale()`/
  `clear_locale()` are a pure data-layer state transition; choosing which files correspond to
  which language stays a caller's job.
- Loading from an Irrlicht-packed archive (`DataManager::LoadDB(IReadFile*)`) is not
  supported; this module reads real filesystem paths only.
- No global SQLite configuration (threading mode, custom VFS) - deliberately, to avoid
  mutating process-wide SQLite state from a library other code in the same process might also
  use.
- Wiring `edopro_next_data` into the legacy `ygoprodll`/premake build is out of scope here.
